# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can feel the three wire positions but have learned no distinguishing properties or safe action. I need the manual’s rule from Mute, and I need Mute to relay Deaf’s visual observations, since Deaf cannot communicate directly with me. I will request both without making an ungrounded cut.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please tell me the manual rule for choosing a wire, and relay Deaf's complete observations of the display, light, and markings.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf reports: display 0; light yellow; wires in order 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue.

Deaf’s report gives me the bomb’s visible state: display 0, yellow light, and wire colours green, yellow, blue in positions 1–3. These observations do not identify the safe cut without the manual’s rule, so I will ask Mute to provide the applicable instruction rather than act.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I received Deaf's report: display 0, yellow light; wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Please give the exact manual instruction and safe wire position.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: display still 0; light is now orange; wires still 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute gestured handshake then upward point.

The only usable new information for me is Deaf’s update: the light changed from yellow to orange, while the display and wire colours remain unchanged. Mute’s gestures are unavailable to me, so they cannot supply the manual rule. I still have no justified wire choice and will not cut one blindly.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot see your gestures. Please speak the exact manual rule and identify the safe wire position for display 0, orange light, and wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Visible state: display 0; wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Light sequence has been yellow, orange, green. Mute's gestures to Deaf across rounds were handshake, upward point, then thumbs-down.

Mute cannot answer in speech, so my earlier request for spoken instructions was unusable. The reported gestures may encode the manual’s result, but I have no established mapping from those gestures to a wire. I will establish a simple relay: Mute should signal the safe position using one unmistakable symbol, and Deaf should report that symbol to me.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please signal only the safe wire position to Deaf: use thumbs-up for wire 1, OK hand for wire 2, or victory sign for wire 3. Deaf, please report exactly which of those three gestures Mute makes.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display 0; wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue; light is yellow again. Mute again gestured thumbs-down.

The light has cycled back to yellow, with the display and wire colours unchanged. Mute’s thumbs-down is not one of the three position codes I requested, so it does not justify cutting any wire. I will ask Mute to distinguish “manual gives no safe cut” from a position, and have Deaf relay the result.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Your thumbs-down is not a wire-position code. If the manual identifies wire 1, gesture thumbs-up; wire 2, gesture OK; wire 3, gesture victory. If none or you cannot determine it, gesture stop with an open palm. Deaf, report Mute's exact gesture.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: display 0; wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue; light orange again. Light sequence so far: yellow, orange, green, yellow, orange. No new gesture from Mute.

The light cycle and fixed wire colours still provide no safe-cut rule by themselves. Mute has not provided a position code; the earlier thumbs-down is not enough to identify a wire. I will restate the code unambiguously and ask Deaf to relay only the resulting symbol.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Use exactly one gesture for the manual's safe wire: thumbs-up means wire 1, OK means wire 2, victory means wire 3. Use open palm only if the manual gives no safe wire. Deaf, report the one gesture you receive.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display 0; wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue; light green. Mute gestured an open raised hand, symbol ?.

Mute’s open raised hand is not one of the position signals previously defined, so I still cannot safely identify a wire. I will use a simpler code that Deaf can report unambiguously: one, two, or three raised fingers correspond to wires 1, 2, or 3. Mute must choose one of those if the manual specifies a cut.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please communicate the manual's required wire using exactly one, two, or three raised fingers: one finger means wire 1, two means wire 2, three means wire 3. Do not use an open hand or any other gesture. Deaf, report the exact number of raised fingers.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display 0; wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue; light yellow. Mute repeated ?.

The bomb remains unchanged, but Mute has still not conveyed a usable wire number. The repeated `?` is not one of the permitted, interpretable position codes, so cutting now would be a guess. I will ask for a three-symbol code using unmistakable listed gestures and have Deaf report the sequence.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please communicate the safe wire with exactly one gesture: thumbs-up means wire 1, OK means wire 2, victory means wire 3. Use no other gesture. Deaf, report which of these three gestures Mute makes, or say unknown.")
wait()
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: display 0; wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue; light orange. Light sequence: yellow, orange, green, yellow, orange, green, yellow, orange. No new gesture.

The light continues its three-state cycle, but the cycle alone does not identify a safe wire. Mute has not sent any recognized position signal, and the reported `?` is not a valid gesture in the defined alphabet. I will not guess or cut a wire. I’ll ask Mute to relay the manual’s literal rule through Deaf using a short, explicit gesture sequence.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please have Deaf relay the manual rule, not a guessed wire: gesture one symbol for display, one for light, then one for the required wire. Use thumbs-up for wire 1, OK for wire 2, victory for wire 3. Deaf, report all three gestures exactly.")
wait()
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Update: display 0; wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue; light green. The light continues the yellow-orange-green cycle. No new gesture.

The bomb’s state is now known, but the manual’s instruction still has not reached me in a decodable form. The repeated open-hand/unknown signalling does not identify a wire, and the light cycle gives no rule by itself. I will ask Mute to send the safe wire as one of three distinct gestures, while also signalling Deaf to report any new instruction rather than another state update.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I still need the manual's exact safe wire. Send exactly one of these: thumbs-up for wire 1, OK for wire 2, victory sign for wire 3. Do not send open hand or unknown.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵"])
wait()
```

TURN 11
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Update: display 0; wires 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue; light yellow. Mute gestured ? ? ?.

Mute’s three gestures still do not identify a wire to me. Since I cannot see gestures, Deaf must relay the result by a spoken description, but Deaf cannot speak or hear; no valid channel has delivered the manual’s rule. The bomb’s observed state alone is insufficient, so any cut would be an unjustified guess.

```text
wait()
```
